description: **Rembrandt van Rijn** is the great painter of the Dutch Golden Age. Self-portraits, biblical scenes and *Night shift*: he paints the human soul.

hero.hook: From the glory of Amsterdam to ruin: a painter who made shadow a language of the soul.

blocks.text: **Rembrandt van Rijn** (1606-1669) is the master of the Dutch school of the 17th century. In the [[The Dutch Golden Age]], the Netherlands becomes a trading power and a hotbed of freedom of thought.
His self-portraits, his biblical scenes and his famous *Night Watch* make chiaroscuro an emotional language. It places humans, splendid or tired, at the center of everything.

In the 17th century, the **United Provinces** dominated world trade. Unlike the rest of Europe, where the Church and kings control art, the Dutch market is driven by a Protestant bourgeoisie. She wants paintings for the house, not church frescoes.
This context favors genres: landscape, still life, everyday scenes. **Vermeer** and  stand out. Rembrandt moved to Amsterdam in **1631** and became the most sought-after portrait painter. [[Hals]]
After his bankruptcy, his son Titus and his partner Hendrickje created an art company of which Rembrandt was officially the employee, to protect his new paintings from creditors.
But his lifestyle is too big. In **1656**, the [[personal bankruptcy]] hits him. House, furniture and collections go to auction. However, he refuses to soften his style to please fashion.

Rembrandt reinvents the [[chiaroscuro]] inherited from the . In his work, the light is not just for show: it seems to filter from within the characters. The gaze focuses on the faces and hands. [[Caravaggio]]

blocks.caption: The Night Watch: a militia in motion, not a fixed alignment.

blocks.text: His other signature: **impasto**, this paint applied so thick that it creates a relief. In an era that wants smooth surfaces, he dares to use materials. It was said that certain portraits could have been lifted by their noses. He seeks the true, not the beautiful ideal.
Chemical analysis revealed plumbonacrit in its impasto: a rare lead compound that helped its thick layers dry faster.

In **1642**, Rembrandt delivers *The Company of Captain Frans Banning Cocq*, known as **Night Watch**. Order for the [[Kloveniersdoelen]], headquarters of a bourgeois militia in Amsterdam. Usually, the militiamen pose in a line, each clearly visible because they have paid.

Rembrandt shows them in movement, leaving the headquarters. The chiaroscuro hierarchizes the figures: some pass into shadow. Legend has it that the furious militiamen caused its downfall. In reality, the work was admired, even if it was confusing.
The title *Night watch* is a misinterpretation: the scene is diurnal. Centuries of dirty varnish have darkened the canvas so much that it looked like a night patrol.
In the 18th century, to install it at the Town Hall, its four sides were cut. Characters disappear. The original composition was much more spacious.

sections.title: The Night Watch: a portrait that moves

blocks.text: Rembrandt painted approximately **80 to 90 self-portraits** over nearly forty years. Young, he appears arrogant, covered in furs and jewelry. After the ruin and the bereavements, the tone changes: more seduction, a raw honesty in the face of aging.

blocks.caption: Late self-portraits: a look without a mask.

blocks.text: Died in **1669**, buried without pomp, he will influence Goya like . He remains the painter who transformed pigment into inner light. [[Francis Bacon]]
Rembrandt magnified human interiority through chiaroscuro and thick paint. From Amsterdam's glory to ruin, his self-portraits remain a unique diary of life.
